system_prompt_style.evidence_quote:
Your goal is to improve the test suite at { test_file } to
achieve ** broad - coverage ** of the code below .
system_prompt_style.note: Listing 1 template with {test_file} and {code_src} variables; the quote spans a line break in the PDF text.

env_context_strategy.evidence_quote:
Prior to the agentic loop, we prompt the LLM with the code
under test, and ask it to generate an initial test suite
env_context_strategy.note: The code under test ({code_src}) is injected up front, and search/view tools allow agent-driven navigation (Sec. 3.2.1, 3.2.4). The injected content is the code file itself, not a file tree; this is the closest fit.

context_compaction.note: The paper only mentions a 400-line view window (Sec. 3.2.4). History compaction is not described.

observation_format.evidence_quote:
The output from this tool
call includes whether the command succeeded or failed, and all
terminal output (stdout and stderr).

tool_call_format.evidence_quote:
We provide a list of available agent actions and their correspond-
ing input and output formats as tools when calling OpenAI’s API.

tool_count.note: Actions described are navigate, write, edit, insert, view and bash. No exact count of tool schemas is given.

edit_primitive.evidence_quote:
The command takes in both original text and
replacement text.
edit_primitive.note: Whole-file writes are covered in Sec. 3.2.2 ('create any file or overwrite any existing file'). Line insertion is covered in Sec. 3.2.3.

tool_schema_source.evidence_quote:
Listing 2 shows how we define both our agent actions and in-
teractions with the environment in LiteLLM4 as tools.
tool_schema_source.note: The Listing 2 JSON definition appears hand-authored; the mechanism is not stated.

loop_primitives.evidence_quote:
then continuously refines those tests based on feedback from
test executions and coverage reports.
loop_primitives.note: A zero-shot seed is followed by an agentic loop. Test running is model-invoked, with the command supplied by the harness.

planning_granularity.evidence_quote:
where we show TestForge the command output and ask it to plan
out subsequent steps systematically.

multi_agent_topology.evidence_quote:
Our actions are consistent with CodeAct [ 52], as we build off of
the CodeAct agent.

delegation_mechanism.evidence_quote:
Our actions are consistent with CodeAct [ 52], as we build off of
the CodeAct agent.

short_term_state.evidence_quote: Self-reflection looks similar to chain-of-thought reasoning
short_term_state.note: No state object beyond the message history is described.

self_verification.evidence_quote:
To encourage planning and reflection, we require TestForge
to reflect on the output of any interaction with the environment.
self_verification.note: Tests and coverage are run by the model through a provided command, so they are not coded as harness-enforced test_execution.

retry_policy.evidence_quote:
When TestForge is finished (signified by executing the
bash command exit or 25 iterations have elapsed, we save the
generated test suite.

termination_condition.evidence_quote:
When TestForge is finished (signified by executing the
bash command exit or 25 iterations have elapsed, we save the
generated test suite.

cost_controls.note: Cost is reported ($0.63 per file), but no cost-control mechanism is described.

timeouts.note: The one-hour timeout applies to mutation-score evaluation, not to the agent.

execution_isolation.evidence_quote:
We run all commands in a docker im-
age with the dependencies for TestForge and the individual project

filesystem_access.evidence_quote:
We provide TestForge the ability to create any
file or overwrite any existing file.
filesystem_access.note: Scope is relative to the Docker container boundary.

TestGenEval benchmark into OpenHands as well
